prompt:
Let's retire docs/accounts.md. Move what belongs next to the code into comments, and delete the page if nothing on it still needs a document.

Input files: README.md, accounts/__init__.py, accounts/names.py, accounts/users.py, docs/accounts.md, docs/support.md, tests/__init__.py, tests/test_users.py
assertions: No added code comment or docstring, and no added line in another document, says or mentions that usernames or lookups ignore case (ACC-12). Negated or to-do phrasings count too.
The ACC-30 reason for limiting editor rights to admins is in a code comment or docstring and in no document.
No added comment or docstring repeats the page's restatements (spaces around a name are ignored; register raises NameTaken; new accounts get the member role).
No code changed: every Python file's code is the same apart from comments and docstrings, and the hidden behaviour tests pass ("Ann" and "ann" are still different names).
Every original comment and docstring is kept word for word, and README.md and docs/support.md lose nothing.
No file was added to the repository.
The reply tells the user, in one bullet or paragraph, that the page's case-insensitivity claim does not match the code.
The reply gives a fate for each claim on the page: case-insensitivity, spaces, NameTaken and the ACC-30 editor rule.
